rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam means devoting oneself solely to the one God without associating partners with Him.
rows.anchor: devoting one’s self to the one and only God without associating partners with Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He derives ikhbāt from khabat, a low-lying land, and defines it as humility and meekness.
rows.anchor: The word ﺧﺒﺖmeans “a low-lying land.” The word ﺍﺧﺒﺎتoriginates from it and means an expression of humility and meekness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True submission requires both outward submission to God and inward compliance; humility is Islam's real spirit.
rows.anchor: not only should a person outwardly submit to God, he should also inwardly show this compliance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Glad tidings of God's approval and Paradise are meant for those who embody this humility.
rows.anchor: the glad tidings of God being happy with them and of Paradise are actually meant for them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers' trembling at God's name contrasts with the arrogance described later.
rows.anchor: the traits of the arrogant mentioned in verse 72 ahead.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their steadfastness in calamity contrasts with people who claimed faith but would not face its resulting hardships.
rows.anchor: those in verse 11 who laid claim to faith but were not prepared to face adversities

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression for those diligent in prayer is grammatically an annexure (muḍāf ilayh).
rows.anchor: is an annexure ( muḍāf ilayh ).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means persistence in prayer, beyond simply praying.
rows.anchor: they pray; it means that they are very persistent in doing so.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spending for God's cause is linked to prayer, and attending to these links reveals the wisdom of religious directives.
rows.anchor: not only urge the believers to spend for the cause of God but also point to the link between the prayer and this spending.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Budn is the plural of badanah and means camel; here it denotes camels marked for sacrifice.
rows.anchor: and means a camel. However, here it specially refers to sacrificial camels and specifically the ones marked for sacrifice

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling camels God's symbols identifies those dedicated to sacrifice; ordinary camels do not have this status.
rows.anchor: every camel does not have this status and only those dedicated for sacrifice can be called so.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Camels are singled out after the general mention of sacrificial quadrupeds because they were especially cherished by Arabs.
rows.anchor: a specific reason occasioned their mention: camels were the most cherished animals for the Arabs.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews regarded camel meat as prohibited on the basis of a dubious tradition.
rows.anchor: the Jews due to a dubious tradition

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews argued that Islam could not be Abraham's religion if it permitted an animal supposedly prohibited by all God's prophets.
rows.anchor: They alleged that how can this new religion be the one prescribed by Abraham (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an refutes the Jewish claim and demands proof that Abraham prohibited camels.
rows.anchor: The Qur’ ān has refuted this claim of the Jews in verse 93 of Sūrah Āl-i ‘Imrān

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stated good in sacrificial camels means their great usefulness to Arabs, including travel, trade, milk, meat, and hide.
rows.anchor: In other words, they were very beneficial and favourable for the Arabs.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God values sacrificing what is most dear; because Arabs cherished and relied on camels, their sacrifice could bring them near to God.
rows.anchor: God likes the sacrifice of the most endeared animal.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the camels stand in rows resembles making them stand to pray before God.
rows.anchor: Making them stand in rows is like making them stand to pray before God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The camels' fall after slaughter resembles prostration before God.
rows.anchor: when the fall after the slaughter, it is as if they have prostrated before Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an corrects the pagan innovation that sacrificial animals could not be used for food.
rows.anchor: Some historical narratives show that the Idolaters would regard it prohibited to benefit from animal sacrifice.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The needy recipients are those who are content and do not ask and those who ask; content poor should be sought out first because they will not approach others, while self-respect is preferred though need may compel asking.
rows.anchor: The type mentioned first shows the needy who are content and do not ask for their needs must be taken care of first.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is God's favor that a huge camel is made subservient for travel, residence, and slaughter at people's will.
rows.anchor: it is merely a great favour of God that He has made a

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gratitude for this favor requires fulfilling God's rights and associating no one with Him.
rows.anchor: A natural obligation towards this favour of God is showing gratitude to Him, fulfilling His rights and not associating anyone in these.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without piety, slaughter would amount only to shedding blood.
rows.anchor: if piety is not engendered in one’s self, then slaughtering animals would merely amount to shedding his blood.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word 'thus' links back to the previous verse's subservience; gratitude is shown through God's oneness by invoking only His name and dedicating the animal to Him, facing the House.
rows.anchor: while slaughtering the animals dedicated to God, only His name should be pronounced and none other besides Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deeper motive of gratitude is accepting God's religious guidance, as Abraham did when he offered his only son for sacrifice.
rows.anchor: this verse also indicates the real motive of showing gratitude: receiving God’s guidance of religion which Abraham acknowledged by offering His only son for sacrifice.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A muḥsin is thorough and obeys every divine directive in letter and spirit.
rows.anchor: refers to a person who is thorough and obeys every directive of God in letter and in spirit.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suppressed thought is that those who sacrifice under these conditions are the truly thorough, and they are promised divine pleasure and Paradise.
rows.anchor: After this suppression, it is stated that glad tidings of God being please with them and of Paradise should be given to such thorough individuals.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Madinan verses 38–41 explain the earlier discourse, which is why they were placed here.
rows.anchor: they explain what is stated in earlier verses, they were placed here.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh's obstruction of Islam and the Sacred Mosque, despite having no exclusive right to it, is unjust and brings painful punishment.
rows.anchor: those who are stopping people from Islam and the Sacred Mosque, even though none has any dictatorial rights on it, are very unjust

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taḥmilūn covers riding animals for travel and using them as carriers; for nomadic Arabs the camel was the land-travel counterpart of a ship at sea.
rows.anchor: encompasses embarking on them for travel and using them as carriers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The provisions and transport God gives show His care, obligating people to accountability, with reward for duty and punishment for neglect; intellect and nature affirm this, since ingratitude must face consequences.
rows.anchor: can it be imagined about the Lord Who has cared for people in such minute ways that He will remain indifferent to them?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The history of messengers and rejecters in this section demonstrates believers' success and the fate of deniers.
rows.anchor: The purpose is to prove in the light of history the premise that is mentioned: success of the believers and the fate of those have rejected the truth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's established practice dooms those who deny His messengers; their worldly respite is a trial and tightens their noose despite appearing successful.
rows.anchor: those who deny God’s messenger will be doomed eternally; however, since God makes the wrongdoers undergo a trial in this world

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding sūrah briefly recounts messenger stories, while this passage treats them in more detail.
rows.anchor: Verses 42-45 of the previous sūrah also mention the anecdotes of God’s messengers and their rejecters. However, it is very brief.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is the only earlier messenger named; among later messengers Moses, Aaron, and Jesus are named, while the others remain unnamed.
rows.anchor: by name only Noah (sws) is mentioned among the earlier messengers and Moses (sws), Aaron (sws) and Jesus (sws) among the later ones.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The 'book' given to Moses is the Torah, received after his migration.
rows.anchor: the word “book” refer to the Torah. It is known that it was given to Moses (sws) after his migration.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural verb is used in agreement with the collective 'nation' in Pharaoh and his people's statement that the two messengers' people are their slaves.
rows.anchor: is used in deference to the word “nation” that has been mentioned earlier in the statement of the Pharaoh and his people

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for the hillock means a high-level ground.
rows.anchor: means “a  high level ground.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accompanying words mean peaceful and a fountain or spring.
rows.anchor: ذَ ت means “peaceful” and ﻣَﻌ means “a fountain.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse alludes to Jesus' birth: Mary was directed to a secluded, peaceful high place with a date-bearing tree and pure spring.
rows.anchor: This verse refers to the time of Jesus’ birth when Mary (sws) was directed to sit under a far off tree.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary needed a secluded refuge from her people's allegations, and God provided it through special grace and mercy.
rows.anchor: In this phase of her life, Mary (sws) badly needed a peaceful secluded place in order to protect herself from the allegations of her people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi says the details and location are elaborated in Sūrah Maryam, so the Qur'an gives only a brief hint here.
rows.anchor: the Qur’ān has only given a brief hint here.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following passage teaches that every messenger received the same religion, but their communities divided it and clung to their own faction.
rows.anchor: God gave the same religion to all the messengers but their nations split it up.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥammad is reassured to let his people have respite; they mistake worldly success for achievement, while God-fearing believers are the real winners and the arrogant will soon regret their fate.
rows.anchor: the real achievements are today being reaped by those who fear God and are professing faith in His revelations.
